summary: Staggered handshake eviction causes cross-variant duplicate routing and mixed model outputs
description:
Issue summary:
Customers on a Dedicated tenant observed intermittent responses that include tokens from two different model variants (13b-v2 and 7b-quant) for the same streaming session. The symptom appears when a staged canary rollout is in progress and when a prewarm/handshake sequence overlaps with an edge retry.

Impact:
- BrightDocs reported 12 user sessions in the last 2 hours that returned mixed-model outputs (semantic drift & hallucination).
- Cost spike: estimated ~18% token cost increase for this tenant during the window due to duplicate processing.
- User-visible: truncated/duplicated paragraphs and inconsistent tone.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dp-az1-us-east (GPU cluster).
- Tenant: brightdocs-prod (dedicated).
- Canary rollout: rolling 20%->40% across a regional shard started 2025-03-01 02:30 UTC.

Observed behavior:
- Requests initially routed to pinned 13b-v2. During prewarm handshake, the orchestrator evicted a stale handshake token and retried via a secondary path that selected 7b-q4_0 as a fallback. The stream merged outputs from both variants (interleaved tokens) and closed with a 200 but inconsistent content.

Expected behavior:
- Pin should be preserved for the session and any edge retries should re-establish the same variant or failover gracefully with whole-response fallback (not interleaved).

Temporary workaround:
- We advised BrightDocs to enable explicit model pin at request-level (model=redwood-open-13b-v2) and disable client-side retries for the streaming route until we stabilize the rollout.

Notes on data sensitivity: customer provided example payloads and first-party sample prompts; no customer PII included in attachments.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a dedicated tenant with a pinned model version (13b-v2) and a staged canary rollout active.
2) Start a streaming session with an initial prompt that triggers >1024 tokens of generation (long response).
3) Induce an edge-level transient by toggling the ingress keepalive headers (simulate reconnect).
4) Observe that the resumed stream includes tokens from an unexpected variant (7b-q4_0) and that logs show two different serving backends handled the same logical session id.

investigation_notes:
Summary of findings:
- Root cause: race between edge prewarm mirror (edge-proxy) and orchestrator's handshake commit. When edge prewarm detects a backend is warm but the orchestrator has not yet committed the cohort snapshot, an eviction path triggers a mirror retry to a candidate variant. Because session ids are reused for streaming reconnects, tokens from both backends can be interleaved into a single logical response.
- Why it escaped earlier tests: this requires a specific timing window created during a staggered canary (partially committed snapshot across shards) plus an ingress reconnect that triggers prewarm mirror.
- Evidence: logs above, ktrace of session handshake (linked), and a spike in duplicated-processing metric in the region dashboard between 02:40-02:50 UTC.
- Related artifacts: slack thread #support (https://slack.redwood/support/threads/CH12345), incident runbook snippet (https://confluence.redwood/runbooks/handshake-eviction), replay traces at tracer.redwood/trace/rd-59f2.
- Hypothesis validated by replay with testrunner: toggling orchestrator snapshot commit delay reproduces behavior deterministically.
resolution_notes:
Work performed so far:
- Fast mitigation: disabled mirror-on-eviction at edge-proxy (hotfix deployed 2025-03-01 11:20 UTC) to prevent secondary-path retries during uncertain handshake state. This reduced duplicated-processing and mixed outputs immediately (~92% reduction).
- Engineering fix: merged PR #4321 that gates mirror retry behind an explicit handshake-consistent flag; extended handshake TTL propagation from orchestrator to edge with a coordinated commit that eliminates the race. Deployed to us-east canary 2025-03-02 09:45 UTC and then rolled region-wide 2025-03-02 11:00 UTC.
- Customer communication: Support notified BrightDocs and recommended re-running affected sessions; offered credits for the cost spike window.
Follow-ups / Action items:
- INT-87412 complete: ensure handshake TTL published in control plane snapshots (done).
- Add synthetic test to the canary harness that simulates prewarm/eviction timing windows (ticket INT-87999).
- Update runbook with diagnostic query and a safe rollback path for mirror logic.
- Postmortem planned; link above.

Current status: Monitoring stable; ticket remains open until postmortem and synthetic tests are added.
